newsitem.title: GERMANY: Debonair adds Germany flights, eyes new destination.
newsitem.headline: Debonair adds Germany flights, eyes new destination.

text.p: Low-cost carrier Debonair Airways will increase domestic German flights from mid-April.
The UK-based start-up airline said it would double flights from Duesseldorf Express airport, Moenchengladbach, to Munich to four a day.
The additional flights would be started as soon as a seventh BAe146-200 aircraft was delivered in four to six week' time, a statement said.
Onward flights to Milan would be started once a second slot had been obtained at Milan airport.
Debonair said it was also considering starting services to Berlin, Hamburg and Hanover from autumn 1997.
The airline currently flies from its Luton airport base to six European destinations and has several cross-border European flights. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax: 5017
